title: Marked semistable alteration of a curve over an arbitrary excellent base
statement:
Let $f:C\to B$ be a proper dominant morphism of integral excellent Noetherian schemes. Suppose its generic fibre has dimension $1$, and let $Z\subset C$ be a proper closed subset. There exist integral excellent Noetherian schemes $C',B'$, alterations $a:C'\to C$ and $b:B'\to B$, and a morphism $f':C'\to B'$ with $fa=bf'$. The morphism $f'$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation. Its geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are nonempty connected reduced curves of pure dimension $1$, smooth except at ordinary double points, and its generic fibre is smooth and geometrically integral. There are finitely many disjoint sections $s_i:B'\to C'$ into the relative smooth locus and a proper closed subset $T\subset B'$ such that $a^{-1}(Z)\subseteq\bigcup_i s_i(B')\cup f'^{-1}(T)$. An ordinary double point has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ on a geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$. An alteration here is a proper surjective morphism finite over a dense open of its integral target. No projectivity or affineness hypothesis on $B$ is imposed.

The notions of proper, integral, excellent, Noetherian, fibre, geometric integrality, dimension, finite morphism and generic point use [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], [def-pc-scheme-fibre], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and [def-sc-generic-point]. Flatness, finite presentation and smoothness use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A section means a morphism $s_i$ with $f's_i=1_{B'}$.

source.place: Theorem 2.4 (i), (ii), and Remark 2.5, printed pp. 602--603, with trivial input group; forget the output group and projectivity. Situation 2.1 allows empty boundary and does not require geometrically irreducible or smooth generic fibre. Local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-excellent-base-generic-curve-preparation] to $f:C\to B$ and $Z$. It gives alterations $a_0:C_0\to C$ and $b_0:B_0\to B$, a proper dominant $f_0$ with $fa_0=b_0f_0$, a smooth geometrically integral generic fibre, and the nowhere-dense reduced boundary $Z_0$ with finite etale generic fibre. No projectivity or separatedness of $B$ or $B_0$ is required.

Apply [lem-trf-dejong-arbitrary-base-marked-semistable] to $(f_0,Z_0)$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1. We obtain integral excellent $C_1,B_1$, alterations $a_1,b_1$, a proper flat finitely presented nodal curve $f_1:C_1\to B_1$, a smooth geometrically integral generic fibre, a proper etale Cartier divisor $D$ in the smooth locus, a nowhere-dense $T_1$, and $a_1^{-1}(Z_0)\subset |D|\cup f_1^{-1}(T_1)$.

Apply [lem-trf-finite-etale-marking-sections] to $g=f_1:C_1\to B_1$ and the divisor $D$ of Step 2; its hypotheses (proper flat finitely presented, integral excellent Noetherian schemes, geometrically integral generic curve, $D$ effective Cartier in the smooth locus and proper etale over $B_1$) are exactly the outputs of [lem-trf-dejong-arbitrary-base-marked-semistable] in Step 2. We get a finite surjective $c:B_2\to B_1$ with $B_2$ integral excellent Noetherian, the base change $C_2=C_1\times_{B_1}B_2$, integral excellent Noetherian, with finite surjective projection $e:C_2\to C_1$ and curve map $f_2:C_2\to B_2$, and sections $s_1,\dots,s_n$ with pairwise disjoint images whose disjoint union is $e^{-1}(D)$, landing in the smooth locus of $f_2$. Put $T=c^{-1}(T_1)$: it is closed, and proper because $c$ is finite dominant between integral schemes, so the generic point of $B_2$ maps to that of $B_1$, which is not in the nowhere-dense $T_1$. Since $|Z_0|=a_0^{-1}(|Z|)$, Step 2 gives $e^{-1}a_1^{-1}a_0^{-1}(Z)\subseteq e^{-1}(|D|)\cup e^{-1}f_1^{-1}(T_1)=\bigcup_is_i(B_2)\cup f_2^{-1}(T)$, using $f_1e=cf_2$.

Set $C'=C_2$, $B'=B_2$, $f'=f_2$, $a=a_0a_1e$ and $b=b_0b_1c$; then $fa=bf'$ by the three commutative squares. Each factor is proper (finite morphisms are proper), so $a,b$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and surjective as composites of surjections. Finiteness over a dense open: if $u:P\to Q$ is finite over a dense open $U\subseteq Q$ and $w:R\to P$ is finite over a dense open $W\subseteq P$, with $P,Q,R$ integral and $u$ dominant, then $u(u^{-1}(U)\setminus W)$ is closed in $U$ (a finite morphism is closed) and omits the generic point of $Q$ (over $U$ the fibre at the generic point of $Q$ is the spectrum of a localization of an affine domain finite over a domain, hence a field: its only point is the generic point of $P$, which lies in the nonempty open $W$); on the dense open $U'=U\setminus u(u^{-1}(U)\setminus W)$ we have $u^{-1}(U')\subseteq W$, so $uw$ is finite over $U'$, affine locally by products of module generators [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Hence $a$ and $b$ are alterations. By [lem-trf-finite-etale-marking-sections](ii), $f'$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation, its generic fibre is smooth and geometrically integral (the base change by a field extension of the smooth geometrically integral generic fibre of $f_1$), and each geometric fibre of $f'$ is a geometric fibre of $f_1$, hence a nonempty connected reduced curve of pure dimension $1$ smooth except at ordinary double points by Step 2. The sections and $T$ come from Step 3, and $C',B'$ are integral excellent Noetherian by Steps 1--3. If $Z=\varnothing$ or $D=\varnothing$, then $n=0$ and the containment is still that of Step 3.

lean.statement: theorem exists_excellentBaseMarkedSemistableCurve {C B : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ B) [IsIntegral C] [IsIntegral B] [IsNoetherian C] [IsNoetherian B] (hC : IsExcellentScheme C) (hB : IsExcellentScheme B) [IsProper f] [IsDominant f] (hgeneric : ∃ η : B, IsGenericPoint η Set.univ ∧ topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber η) = 1) (Z : Set C) (hZ : IsClosed Z ∧ Z ≠ Set.univ) : ∃ (C' B' : Scheme.{u}) (a : C' ⟶ C) (b : B' ⟶ B) (f' : C' ⟶ B'), a ≫ f = f' ≫ b ∧ IsIntegral C' ∧ IsExcellentScheme C' ∧ IsNoetherian C' ∧ IsIntegral B' ∧ IsExcellentScheme B' ∧ IsNoetherian B' ∧ (IsProper a ∧ Surjective a ∧ (∃ U : C.Opens, Dense (U : Set C) ∧ IsFinite (pullback.snd a U.ι))) ∧ (IsProper b ∧ Surjective b ∧ (∃ U : B.Opens, Dense (U : Set B) ∧ IsFinite (pullback.snd b U.ι))) ∧ IsProper f' ∧ Flat f' ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f' ∧ QuasiCompact f' ∧ QuasiSeparated f' ∧ (∀ y : B', IsSemistableGeometricCurve (pullback.snd f' (geometricPoint B' y))) ∧ (∃ η' : B', IsGenericPoint η' Set.univ ∧ Smooth (f'.fiberToSpecResidueField η') ∧ GeometricallyIntegral (f'.fiberToSpecResidueField η')) ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, ∃ s : Fin n → (B' ⟶ C'), ∃ T : Set B', (∀ i : Fin n, s i ≫ f' = 𝟙 B') ∧ (∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → Disjoint (Set.range (s i)) (Set.range (s j))) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, ∀ x : C', x ∈ Set.range (s i) → (f'.stalkMap x).hom.FormallySmooth) ∧ (IsClosed T ∧ T ≠ Set.univ) ∧ a ⁻¹' Z ⊆ (⋃ i : Fin n, Set.range (s i)) ∪ f' ⁻¹' T)
